title: Passive: Present and Past Simple
summary: Use the passive to say what happens to a person or thing when the action is more important than the person doing it. Form present and past simple passive sentences, negatives and questions.
learningObjectives: Change a simple active statement into a present or past simple passive statement.
Choose am/is/are or was/were with a past participle to match the subject and time.
Form passive negatives and questions and use by to name the person who did the action.
Use was born and were born when speaking about birth.

explanation.heading: Focus on the person or thing affected
explanation.body: An active sentence usually starts with the person doing an action. A passive sentence starts with the person or thing receiving the action. You can leave out the doer when it is unknown, obvious or unimportant.
explanation.example: A volunteer sorts the donations. The donations are sorted by a volunteer.

explanation.heading: Present simple passive
explanation.body: Use am, is or are + the past participle for routine actions and general facts. Choose the form of be to agree with the subject. Regular past participles usually end in -ed; some verbs have irregular forms, such as made and written.
explanation.example: Fresh bread is delivered to the café each morning.

explanation.heading: Past simple passive
explanation.body: Use was or were + the past participle for completed actions in the past. Was goes with singular subjects; were goes with plural subjects and you. The past participle does not change for singular or plural subjects.
explanation.example: The old seats were replaced last spring.

explanation.heading: Negatives and questions
explanation.body: For negatives, put not after the form of be: is not, are not, was not or were not. For questions, put the form of be before the subject. You can also begin with a question word, such as when or where.
explanation.example: Were the documents signed yesterday? No, they were not signed.

explanation.heading: Born and by
explanation.body: Use was born or were born when talking about where or when people came into the world. If you need to identify the person who did a passive action, add by + that person after the verb phrase.
explanation.example: Leo was born in Cardiff. His first bicycle was made by his uncle.

left.label: Active
left.example: The chef prepares the soup every morning.
left.note: The chef is the subject and performs the action.

right.label: Passive
right.example: The soup is prepared every morning.
right.note: The soup is the subject and receives the action.

left.label: Present routine
left.example: The hall is used for dance classes on Mondays.
left.note: Is used describes a regular situation.

right.label: Completed past action
right.example: The hall was used for a concert last Monday.
right.note: Was used refers to a particular past time.

examples.sentence: The rubbish bins are emptied every Thursday.
examples.note: Plural present simple passive for a routine.

examples.sentence: This song was written by my neighbour.
examples.note: Past simple passive with by to identify the writer.

examples.sentence: We are not allowed to bring food into the studio.

examples.note: A past passive question with a question word.

examples.sentence: My twins were born in September.
examples.note: Were born agrees with a plural subject.

commonMistakes.incorrect: The signs is checked each morning.
commonMistakes.correct: The signs are checked each morning.
commonMistakes.why: The plural subject signs needs are.

commonMistakes.incorrect: The parcel was send on Tuesday.
commonMistakes.correct: The parcel was sent on Tuesday.
commonMistakes.why: A passive verb needs a past participle, not the base form.
In a direct question, were comes before you.

commonMistakes.incorrect: The portrait painted by my sister last year.
commonMistakes.correct: The portrait was painted by my sister last year.
commonMistakes.why: The past passive requires was or were before painted.

studyTips: First identify the subject: is it doing the action or receiving it?
When you see a past time such as last month, check whether was or were is needed.
Learn irregular past participles in useful pairs: send–sent, make–made and write–written.

exercises.prompt: Each evening, the library doors ___ at six.
exercises.feedback: The plural subject doors takes are; each evening indicates a routine, so use the present simple passive.

exercises.prompt: Last Saturday, the market stalls ___ early because of the storm.
exercises.feedback: Last Saturday requires the past simple, and plural stalls takes were closed.
Yesterday makes this a past question, and plural invitations requires Were.
Use was born with a singular subject when asking about someone’s birthplace.

exercises.prompt: Complete with the present simple passive of 'check': These bikes ___ before every tour.
acceptedAnswers: are checked
exercises.feedback: These bikes is plural and before every tour describes a regular action: are checked.

exercises.prompt: Complete with the past simple passive of 'build': The wooden stage ___ in 2018.
acceptedAnswers: was built
exercises.feedback: A single stage takes was, and the irregular past participle of build is built.

exercises.prompt: Complete with the negative present simple passive of 'serve': Hot meals ___ after nine in the evening at this café.
acceptedAnswers: are not served
aren't served
exercises.feedback: Plural meals requires are not served or its contraction; the instruction specifies a negative.

exercises.prompt: Complete with the missing word: The song was written ___ her older brother.
acceptedAnswers: by
exercises.feedback: By introduces the person who wrote the song.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: The photos is printed at the shop every Monday.
acceptedAnswers: The photos are printed at the shop every Monday.
exercises.feedback: Photos is plural, so the present passive needs are.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: Our team shirts were make last year.
acceptedAnswers: Our team shirts were made last year.
exercises.feedback: Use the irregular past participle made after were.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: My sister is born in June 2005.
acceptedAnswers: My sister was born in June 2005.
exercises.feedback: Use was born to give a person’s date of birth.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: Was the packages delivered this morning?
acceptedAnswers: Were the packages delivered this morning?
exercises.feedback: The plural noun packages requires Were at the beginning of the question.

speakingExercises.prompt: Say one complete sentence in the present simple passive using: 'our recycling bins / empty / every Tuesday'.
acceptedAnswers: Our recycling bins are emptied every Tuesday.
speakingExercises.feedback: The regular action uses are + emptied with plural bins.

speakingExercises.prompt: Say one complete sentence in the past simple passive using: 'the school gate / paint / last weekend'.
acceptedAnswers: The school gate was painted last weekend.
speakingExercises.feedback: Use was painted for the single gate and the completed past action.

speakingExercises.prompt: Answer with a complete sentence: 'Where was Nora born?' Use the information 'Nora / born / in Bristol'.
acceptedAnswers: Nora was born in Bristol.
She was born in Bristol.
speakingExercises.feedback: Use was born for one person and give the city in a full sentence.

speakingExercises.prompt: The school hall is used on weekdays but not on Sundays. Say a negative present simple passive sentence about Sundays. Start with 'The school hall'.
acceptedAnswers: The school hall is not used on Sundays.
The school hall isn't used on Sundays.
speakingExercises.feedback: Use is not used (or isn't used) to describe a regular negative passive situation.

speakingExercises.prompt: Change this active sentence into the past simple passive: 'An artist painted the mural last summer.' Start with 'The mural' and include who painted it and when.
acceptedAnswers: The mural was painted by an artist last summer.
The mural was painted last summer by an artist.
speakingExercises.feedback: Was painted is the past passive; by an artist identifies the person who did the work.

speakingExercises.prompt: A customer asks, 'Was the parcel sent yesterday?' The answer is yes. Reply in a complete sentence beginning 'Yes, the parcel'. Include 'yesterday'.
acceptedAnswers: Yes, the parcel was sent yesterday.
speakingExercises.feedback: Use was sent for a single parcel and a completed action yesterday.

speakingExercises.prompt: Correct only the verb agreement in this sentence and say it in full: 'These letters was sent yesterday.'
acceptedAnswers: These letters were sent yesterday.
speakingExercises.feedback: Plural letters requires were, not was, before the past participle sent.

speakingExercises.prompt: Give two short passive sentences about a community hall. First, its windows are cleaned every Friday. Second, its doors were repaired last week. Start with 'The windows' and then 'The doors'.
acceptedAnswers: The windows are cleaned every Friday. The doors were repaired last week.
speakingExercises.feedback: Use are cleaned for a routine and were repaired for a completed action in the past.

listeningExercises.audioText: The front doors are unlocked at eight every weekday.
listeningExercises.prompt: What happens to the front doors?
choices: They are unlocked regularly at eight.
listeningExercises.feedback: Are unlocked and every weekday describe a regular action, not a single past event.

listeningExercises.audioText: The picnic tables were moved indoors after the rain began.
listeningExercises.prompt: What happened to the picnic tables?
choices: They are moved indoors every day.
They were made after the rain.
They were moved indoors in the past.
listeningExercises.feedback: Were moved is past simple passive: the tables received the action.

listeningExercises.audioText: My aunt was born in a small town near York.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the missing word in the phrase 'My aunt ___ born in a small town near York.'
acceptedAnswers: was
listeningExercises.feedback: Was born is the past passive expression used for one person’s birth.

listeningExercises.audioText: At the market, fresh vegetables are delivered before sunrise every morning.
listeningExercises.prompt: What happens regularly at the market?
choices: Vegetables arrive before the sun comes up.
Customers take vegetables home after dark.
The market closes as soon as the deliveries arrive.
listeningExercises.feedback: Are delivered and every morning describe a routine; before sunrise tells us when it happens.

listeningExercises.audioText: The winning poster was designed by a student from our school last winter.
choices: Someone who studies at the school.
listeningExercises.feedback: By a student identifies the person who designed the poster.

listeningExercises.audioText: The bakery windows are cleaned every Monday, but the front door was repaired last Thursday.
listeningExercises.prompt: Which job was completed on a specific day in the past?
choices: The regular cleaning of the windows.
Fixing the entrance to the bakery.
listeningExercises.feedback: Was repaired last Thursday refers to one completed past job, unlike the routine cleaning.

listeningExercises.audioText: The painting was sold at an auction on Saturday afternoon.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the two-word past passive verb phrase you hear about the painting.
acceptedAnswers: was sold
listeningExercises.feedback: Was sold is the past simple passive: was plus the past participle sold.

listeningExercises.audioText: Local newspapers are printed at this factory every afternoon.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the two-word present passive verb phrase you hear.
acceptedAnswers: are printed
listeningExercises.feedback: Are printed is the present simple passive for the plural subject newspapers.
